newsitem.title: ITALY: Deputy PM calls for shake up of Italian welfare.
newsitem.headline: Deputy PM calls for shake up of Italian welfare.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni at the weekend called for a shake-up of the Italian welfare state, saying the government should tackle the problem as soon as the 1997 budget had been approved by parliament.
Veltoni told a conference of Italian business leaders that the welfare system must be made more efficient.
"As soon as the budget is out of the way, we will join with unions, employees and parliament to work together on a welfare state for the year 2000," he said.
He also said that a review of Italy's 1995 pension reform should be brought forward a year to 1997 if unions agreed.
However Sergio D'Antoni, the leader of Italy's second largest union, said he was opposed to any early review.
"If the government insists on bringing forward this review to 1997 then it really risks a serious break (with the unions)," D'Antoni said in an interview with daily Corriere della Sera.
The hardleft Communist Refoundation, which supports Italy's centre-left government and guarantees its majority in the lower house of parliament, also rejected the idea.
"We're not even going to talk about it," Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
